name: Guyana

findings.summary: Huawei built Guyana's state e-government network (Georgetown fibre and a coastal 4G LTE network, about US$32m); in January 2017 Cabinet approved a Huawei programme to replace hardware, update software and provide remote support.
findings.analyst_inference: Equipment vendor and ongoing software/support provider is Huawei, so prc. Tier 5: the 2018 editorial describes the network as in use serving schools and agencies. Original build date not established (under the pre-2015 PPP/C government); finding dated to the 2017 support approval. US$32m is the editorial's figure. HGPTV (2023) reports the Vice-President defending continued Huawei ICT use, suggesting but not confirming still_current.

findings.local_actor: Government of Guyana (Ministry of Public Communications) / NDMA
findings.summary: National Broadband Expansion Project: Huawei's US$37.6m contract to expand the state LTE network and e-government services, financed by a China Eximbank concessional loan signed October 2018; about 96% disbursed by end-2020.
findings.analyst_inference: Tier 4 because the loan is signed and largely disbursed (AidData); completion of the LTE component not confirmed. Huawei is equipment vendor, so prc. AidData compiles the loan agreement and official sources; tiered S2 as a specialist research dataset.

findings.local_actor: Government of Guyana / Guyana Police Force
findings.summary: The same Huawei broadband contract covered a safe-city component: more CCTV cameras nationwide, a CCTV command centre, a police patrol-tracking centre and a unified emergency call centre; AidData reports the safe-city part largely complete by late 2019.
findings.analyst_inference: Huawei supplies and integrates the system, so prc. Coded tier 4 (financing closed); 'largely complete' rests on AidData alone, so tier 5 not claimed. Camera brand not named. AidData notes local concern over facial recognition and possible Huawei access to government data.

findings.summary: The Huawei broadband project included upgrading the government data centre at Castellani House and building a second, backup government data centre, financed by the China Eximbank loan.
findings.analyst_inference: Building owner-operator is the Guyanese state (NDMA), so domestic per v0.2; Huawei is builder/equipment supplier and China Eximbank the financier. Backup data centre completion not confirmed.

findings.summary: Government-run Safe Country surveillance network: about 6,000 cameras installed, regional command centres operating, AI traffic cameras deployed; President Ali plans 20,000 more cameras plus facial recognition and predictive policing by 2030. Vendor not disclosed.
findings.analyst_inference: Pole null: no camera, software or integrator vendor named in any opened source. Guyana Chronicle is state-owned, so S4; the High Commission page reprints domestic state reporting (January 2024: command centres in Regions 3 and 6 partly operating). Relation to the Huawei safe-city component (GUY-003) not established. Budget figures are in Guyana dollars and not converted.

findings.summary: Government of Guyana and Cerebras signed an MOU for Cerebras to build and operate an AI data centre of up to 100MW at Wales, beside a gas-to-energy plant with behind-the-meter power; no value or timeline given.
findings.analyst_inference: Cerebras (US) to build and operate, so us; ownership structure undisclosed. Tier 1 (MOU). A February 2026 ministerial speech (DPI) said data-centre letters of intent were still under review, so no advance beyond MOU is evidenced.

findings.summary: Under the same MOU Cerebras said it would deploy its CS-3 AI systems in the planned Wales data centre, framed under its Cerebras for Nations sovereign-AI programme.
findings.analyst_inference: US accelerator vendor, so us. Tier 1; no shipment or export licence evidenced.

models.null_reason: one search and a February 2026 ministerial speech found no frontier-provider partnership or national model

power.null_reason: the Wales gas-to-energy plant is a grid project; behind-the-meter data-centre supply exists only as part of the Cerebras MOU (GUY-006)

research_gaps: Radio/core vendors of commercial operators GTT and Digicel Guyana not established (one search found nothing).
Is the Huawei e-government network still Huawei-supported, and was the NBEP LTE and backup data centre completed?
Camera, video-analytics and integrator vendors of the Safe Country network (about 6,000 cameras, AI traffic cameras); link to the Huawei safe-city component?
Has the Cerebras Wales MOU progressed to a contract, site works or export licence; who owns the facility?
Submarine cables (HMN Tech involvement) not searched; no Huawei/ZTE ban or reversal found in one search.
